blocks.text: Chilliwack Mobile & Manufactured Homes for Sale

parts.t: Chilliwack's mobile home parks offer accessible housing in a beautiful Fraser Valley setting with mountain views and outdoor recreation access. These affordable options attract first-time buyers, retirees, and anyone seeking lower-cost living without sacrificing community atmosphere or quality of life. Many parks feature well-maintained properties with modern amenities, mature landscaping, and friendly neighbors creating genuine community connections.

Residents enjoy Chilliwack's natural beauty with hiking, fishing, and water sports nearby, plus convenient access to shopping, services, and healthcare facilities. The city's growing economy, improving infrastructure, and family-friendly amenities make it increasingly popular among those leaving expensive Metro Vancouver markets. Mobile home living provides ownership pride with reduced maintenance responsibilities and lower costs, freeing up resources for hobbies and recreation. Parks vary in age, amenities, and pad rental fees, making careful selection important. blocks.text: Buying a Mobile or Manufactured Home in Chilliwack & Sardis

parts.t: Chilliwack and Sardis have one of the largest selections of manufactured and modular homes in the Fraser Valley, providing single-level detached living at a fraction of the price of a conventional detached house. Listings fall into two main legal structures:
pad-rental manufactured home parks
(governed by BC's
Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act
or First Nations lease agreements, where you purchase the home and pay a monthly pad fee) and
freehold or bare-land strata manufactured home communities
(where you own the lot or strata share alongside the home).

blocks.text: Chilliwack Mobile & Manufactured Homes Real Estate FAQs

parts.t: What is the difference between a pad-rental park and a bare-land strata mobile home in Chilliwack?

In a pad-rental park, you buy the manufactured home itself (registered in the BC Manufactured Home Registry) and pay a monthly pad rent for the site and utilities such as water, sewer, and garbage. In a bare-land strata community, you own the land parcel in fee simple and pay a smaller monthly strata fee for common roads and amenities.
What do monthly pad rental fees cost in Chilliwack manufactured home parks?

Monthly pad fees in Chilliwack and Sardis manufactured home parks typically range from $550 to $950 per month depending on the park, location, and whether municipal water, sewer, garbage pickup, snow removal, and clubhouse access are included.
Why do lenders check for a CSA Z240 label or Technical Safety BC Silver Label?

Mortgage lenders and insurance underwriters require proof that a manufactured home meets safety standards via its factory CSA Z240 MH (or A277) data plate and sticker, or a Technical Safety BC Silver Label confirming the electrical system has been inspected and approved.
How does financing work for a mobile home on a rented pad vs. owned land?

Manufactured homes on owned bare-land strata lots qualify for standard residential mortgages, while homes on rented pads require specialized chattel/leasehold manufactured-home financing through lenders such as RBC, regional credit unions, or CMHC-insured chattel programs (which evaluate the home's age, CSA label, and park tenancy assignment).
Are there 55+ manufactured home parks in Sardis and Chilliwack?

Yes. Many manufactured home parks in Sardis, Promontory, Vedder, and Bridal Falls enforce 55+ age rules (which remain legal under BC tenancy and strata legislation), while select parks allow all-age occupancy.
Do you pay BC Property Transfer Tax on a mobile home in a pad-rental park?

If you are buying only a manufactured home located on a rented pad (with no registered freehold or registrable long-term lease interest transferred at the Land Title Office), BC Property Transfer Tax generally does not apply; the ownership transfer is filed through the BC Manufactured Home Registry.
What should I check before removing subjects on a Chilliwack manufactured home?

Confirm park management approval and park rules (pets, age limits, fencing, parking), verify the BC Manufactured Home Registry (MHR) number and clear liens via a personal property registry search, check the CSA/Silver Label, and inspect the roof, poly-B plumbing (if built in the late 1980s–1990s), skirting, and belly wrap.
